title: Comparison of different therapeutic algorithms in late abortions - a retrospective study based on patient cohorts from two clinics
summary:
This study looks at miscarriages that occur between the 11th and 23rd week of pregnancy. These events affect about 2–3% of pregnancies, and treatment approaches can vary between hospitals. The goal of this project is to find out which treatment strategy is both best for patients and uses medical resources efficiently.
To do this, medical records from two hospitals—University Hospital Münster and Florence Nightingale Hospital Düsseldorf—will be analyzed. The study includes adult patients whose pregnancies ended in an early or late miscarriage.
Researchers will collect information such as the mother’s age, the timing of the diagnosis and miscarriage, possible complications, existing health conditions, and how long the hospital stay lasted.
By analyzing these data, the study aims to improve treatment decisions, avoid unnecessary procedures, and support better counseling for patients in the future.
conditions: Unspecified abortion: Complete or unspecified, without complication

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all female patients aged ≥18 years who were admitted to the Florence Nightingale Hospital Düsseldorf between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024, and who experienced a late miscarriage between 11+0 and 23+6 weeks of gestation.

A retrospective analysis was conducted including all female patients aged 18 years or older who were admitted to the University Hospital Münster between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024, and who experienced a late miscarriage between 11+0 and 23+6 weeks of gestation.
